A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Compositional Risk Minimization and contain readable main text and appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite additions and repagination.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations and Gaussian simulations in Section 4 and Appendices E and G.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark evaluations, ablations and Gaussian simulations in Section 5 and Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: The additive energy classifier, training objective, bias extrapolation and inference procedure remain unchanged in Equations 7–11 and Algorithms 1–2. Section 3.4 explains the existing method without modifying its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Waterbirds, CelebA, MetaShift, MultiNLI, CivilComments and NICO++, including the five-attribute CelebA variant and synthetic Gaussian scenarios. Appendix B's added CivilComments example is explanatory, not additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ERM, GroupDRO, LC, sLA, IRM, VREx and Mixup, with the same subset in Table 1. Newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The group-removal procedure, NICO++ filtering, data splits, accuracy metrics, model backbones, optimizers and hyperparameter searches are retained. Appendix F documents the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the bias and prior ablations, Gaussian comparison with ERM, and group-coverage sensitivity analyses. The numerical corrections do not introduce or change the tested ablation comparisons or supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both report results over three random seeds with the same standard-error reporting practice. Some error values change, but no repeated-run count or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes learned-bias CRM WGA from 29.2 to 30.4 on MultiNLI and 51.9 to 52.4 on CivilComments; full CRM changes from 57.7 to 58.7 and 68.1 to 67.9, respectively. Several Table 2 standard errors also change, and Table 13 changes CRM's MetaShift standard error from 0.7 to 0.4. Table 1 and the substantive performance conclusions are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an explicit definition and groupwise decomposition of compositional risk in Equation 14, relating its minimization to Bayes optimality. Equations 12–13 restate identities already derived in v2 Appendix D.2; the existing assumptions, theorems and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and central conclusion retain the same claims: tractable discriminative CRM, extrapolation within discrete affine hulls, rapid hull growth and empirical robustness under compositional shifts.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly explains why affine combinations of energies do not imply affine mixtures of densities and why the classifier avoids explicit affine-weight estimation. The conclusion explicitly identifies reliance on labeled attributes as a practical limitation, while Appendix B expands the conceptual examples.

D1.justification: V3 adds a first-page code-repository link absent from v2. The in-document implementation in Appendix C and experimental details in Appendix F remain unchanged; repository contents or availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds Qiao and Peng (2023) and Yao et al. (2023). Section 3.4 uses these references alongside Krueger et al. (2021) to contrast AED assumptions with approaches based on convex or affine hulls of training distributions.

P1.justification: V3 adds a numbered Introduction, a Further Insights subsection and a Limitations paragraph, expands Appendix B, and makes localized wording, heading and cross-reference corrections. Most prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: All nine figures and fourteen tables retain their basic designs. V3 updates table captions and the MultiNLI header, adjusts the title block, and reflows existing material, including Figures 5–6 relative to surrounding proof text.

improvement.justification: V3 improves clarity through Section 3.4 and the explicit attribute-label limitation, adds code access information, and reconciles several Table 2 entries with results already reported elsewhere. These are useful but limited improvements. Numerical consistency remains incomplete: Waterbirds and CelebA standard errors still disagree between Tables 2 and 13.
